chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

'Abdullah ibn Muhammad wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him): Some of our companions reported from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the man who divorces his wife upon the Book and the Sunnah, so she becomes irrevocably divorced from him with one (divorce). So she marries another husband, and he dies from her, or divorces her, she can return to her former husband, for her to be with him upon two divorces and one (of it) having expired.
So he (peace be upon him) signed with his own handwriting: 'They speak the truth'.

And some of them had reported that she would happen to be with him upon three future divorces, and that which he had divorced her with would not be with anything, because she had married another husband.
So he (peace be upon him) signed with his own handwriting: 'No'.

key_terms.عَلَى الْكِتَابِ وَ السُّنَّةِ: Upon the Book and the Sunnah (a formula of divorce)

ai.seo_question: Does a prior divorce count towards the three divorces required for a woman to be permanently forbidden to her first husband after a second marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi addresses the specific legal nuance of 'Talaq al-Kutub wa al-Sunnah' (divorce according to the Book and the Sunnah), where a husband pronounces three divorces at once. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the view that the first divorce is effective immediately upon the second husband's death or divorce, leaving the woman with two future divorces, while rejecting the view that the initial pronouncement is nullified by the intervening marriage. This ruling highlights the Shia emphasis on the immediate efficacy of the first divorce in a triple pronouncement, distinguishing it from the Hanafi practice of treating them as a single irrevocable block.
